newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile phone rings off hook with PGM calls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile phone rings off hook with PGM calls.

text.p: U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center said it has been fending off calls from people desperate to get their hands on some of the U.S. government's hoard of white metals as prices climb through the roof.
"The question is, who has not called," said Peter Roman, Stockpile's marketing manager.
Stockpile sold its first batch of white metals quickly earlier this year after 10,000 ounces of platinum and 15,000 ounces of palladium went on the block.
This was just a tiny part of Stockpile's platinum and palladium reserves of 431,760 ounces and 1,264,601 ounces, respectively.
Some of the metal went at a premium to the London white metal fixings despite dealers scoffing initially at Stockpile's hopes of avoiding sales at a discount to this benchmark.
But Russia's failure to export any white metals so far this year along with a short wildcat strike at a key South Africa mine boosted prices as spot supplies shrivelled.
Palladium has rocketed to 17-year highs, and the cost of borrowing the white metals has also soared.
"Regrettably, we are not in the market," Roman said.
Even if Stockpile began taking steps now to begin extra sales, any offering would not take place before the end of summer even if Congress gave the nod, Roman added.
